title: Supplement: LFP bad-channel/bad-trial detection via channel correlation and consensus cross-channel artifact detection
notes: Hamm's ask (2026-08-17): supplement reporting %% trials/channels excluded per monkey/session for LFP artifact rejection, plus document the channel-exclusion method (partial correlation across channels to find deviant/damaged/detached-contact channels). Explore-agent search first confirmed neither piece existed anywhere in the repo -- no partial-correlation channel QC, no deviant-channel detection, no corpus-wide trial-exclusion table. The 'artifact rejection = 6x RMS, ~40/960 trials' claim in context/analysis_spec_SPK.md SS0.2 has no code behind it in this repo.

Built jnwb/artifact_detection.py: channel_correlation_matrix + bad_channels_from_correlation (channel x channel Pearson correlation, MAD-based low-outlier per-channel summary flag); trial_correlation_matrix + bad_trials_single_channel (trial x trial Pearson correlation per good channel, low-correlation OR high-amplitude MAD-outlier flag); consensus_bad_trials (a trial excluded only if flagged on >=50%% of a session's good channels independently, implementing Hamm's 'artifacts appear in all good channels always, if they exist').

tests/test_artifact_detection.py, 7/7 passing: synthetic bad-channel recovery with zero false positives; synthetic bad-trial recovery (5/5 injected artifacts, near-zero false positives among 95 clean trials); consensus correctly rejects a single-channel-only flag and accepts a 5/6-channel shared flag; determinism (pure function of input).

PERFORMANCE BUG found and fixed during build: initial per-channel full-trace h5py reads (data[:, ch] for each of 128 channels) took ~30s EACH because this dataset is chunked across the full channel width per time-block, so a single-column read forces decompressing every channel's data. Fixed by reading each trial window across ALL channels at once (matches _l_lfp_common.extract_epoch_trials' existing pattern) -- reduced a single-session smoke test from a >5min stall (still not finished) to 30-99s.

SEPARATE BUG found and fixed: probe_channel_range initially returned GLOBAL electrode-table row indices (e.g. probe B = rows 128-256) and used them directly as column indices into that probe's OWN LFP dataset, which is independently 0-based per probe (each probe_N_lfp array is its own (n_samples, 128) array, not a slice of one shared (n_samples, 384) array). This silently produced empty (0-width) slices for every non-first probe -- confirmed via 'Mean of empty slice' RuntimeWarnings and n_bad_channels=0/n_good_channels_used=NaN for probes B/C on the first smoke test. Fixed to return (0, n_channels) local to each probe's own dataset.

POSITIVE CONTROL: this corpus's own prior documented finding (jnwb/artifact_repair.py's receipt) is that raw-LFP movement artifacts are a V182o/V198o phenomenon, not C31o. This detector reproduces that asymmetry from raw data with no prior knowledge encoded in the method: mean %% bad trials per session = Cajal/C31o 0.10%%, Ivan/V182o 7.86%%, Joule/V198o 2.96%%. Confirms specificity, not just sensitivity to injected synthetic artifacts.

FULL CORPUS RESULT (22/22 sessions, 71 session-probe rows, ~33 min runtime): pooled %% channels excluded = Cajal 3.98%%, Ivan 5.76%%, Joule 8.95%%. pooled %% trials excluded (consensus) = Cajal 0.10%%, Ivan 7.86%% (pooled 7.86%%), Joule 2.09%% (pooled; mean-of-sessions 2.96%%, session-count-weighted differs because sessions have different trial counts).

Figure built (supplement_lfp_artifact_qc.py): per-session bar charts, %% trials and %% channels excluded, colored by monkey, per-monkey mean dashed line. Two layout bugs found and fixed via the mandatory visual-inspection step (omission-figures skill: 'export without looking is not verification') -- legend clipped off the top of the canvas on the first render, then legend/suptitle overlapping on the second; fixed via explicit y-position tuning for legend vs suptitle vs subplots_adjust top/bottom margins.
issues: Channel QC uses only a 120s continuous segment per probe (not the full recording) -- a channel that degrades partway through a session would not be caught.

Trial QC window (-200..+800 ms around p1 onset) does not cover the full ~4.6s trial -- chosen for tractable runtime on a 22-session corpus at 'quickly implement' priority, not because later trial epochs are known artifact-free.

z=5.0 and 50%% consensus threshold are defensible round numbers, not tuned against a labeled ground-truth artifact set (none exists in this corpus). The positive-control asymmetry supports rough calibration but is not a formal sensitivity/specificity analysis.

Not yet reconciled with the EXISTING jnwb/artifact_repair.py sample-level repair mechanism -- this is trial-level EXCLUSION, a different action from interpolation/substitution within a kept trial. Whether to run repair-then-exclude, exclude-then-repair, or pick one exclusively is an open design question.
